technology: Low-input Han / Roman / Parthian agriculture, approximately 200 AD
interpretation: Population scenarios, not a reconstructed census or a validated demographic forecast
assumptions: Crop yields, arable fractions, irrigation reach, fallow and calorie needs are inherited from the Harvest food model; they are low-input period assumptions.
Occupation scenarios are quantiles of historical population / food-capacity ratios in the existing Earth comparison, excluding the fitted Han plains. They are analogues, not confidence limits.
Biome crop realization represents clearing and management effort. Its coefficients are explicit scenario choices, not measured biome fertility or published 200 AD population coefficients.
Waterway access is a settlement scenario modifier; irrigation is already represented separately in crop yields.
The grazing calculation is a forage-energy allowance on land reserved from cropping. Aboveground, edible forage and human calorie conversion shares are uncertain scenario assumptions.
Mordecai 2013 Table 2 and equation 2 supply the malaria thermal traits. The curve is normalized against a fixed temperature grid, not each map.
Rainfall and irrigation are a simple moisture gate added to the thermal model. Relative suitability is not prevalence, mortality, or the probability of infection.
The maximum 35% disease penalty is a scenario assumption. An absent-malaria scenario removes it entirely.
Cities, food imports, fishing, soil nutrients, flood damage, political history and epidemic shocks are not explicitly simulated.
